data.title: Methylprednisolone (IV pulse)
data.summary: II Corticosteroids · Intermediate-acting glucocorticoid; methylprednisolone sodium succinate for IV use
data.body:
_Injectables · II Corticosteroids_

**Class:** Intermediate-acting glucocorticoid; methylprednisolone sodium succinate for IV use

## Mechanism of action
- At pulse doses, genomic effects are saturated and rapid non-genomic effects on cell membranes add to immunosuppression
- Rapid lymphocyte depletion and suppression of inflammation — gives quick disease control with fewer long-term side effects than prolonged high oral doses

## Pharmacokinetics
- Equivalence: 4 mg methylprednisolone = 5 mg prednisolone
- Minimal mineralocorticoid effect, so preferred for pulse therapy
- Methylprednisolone acetate (depot) is a different, long-acting IM/IL suspension — never give it IV

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Pemphigus vulgaris/foliaceus (severe, not responding), bullous pemphigoid (severe)
- SJS/TEN (early, short course — controversial), DRESS (severe), severe erythema multiforme
- Pyoderma gangrenosum, dermatomyositis (severe/with lung involvement), vasculitis, SLE
- Rapidly progressive alopecia areata (selected), severe type 1 lepra reaction or ENL with neuritis

## Dose & formulations
- Pulse: 500 mg–1 g (about 10–15 mg/kg/day) in 250–500 mL of 5% dextrose or normal saline over 1–3 h, daily for 3 (to 5) consecutive days
- Never as a rapid IV bolus (risk of arrhythmia and sudden death)
- Follow with oral steroid or steroid-sparing drug
- Vials 40, 125, 500 mg, 1 g

## Adverse effects
- Acute: flushing, metallic taste, hyperglycaemia, hypertension, insomnia, mood change, psychosis
- Electrolyte shifts (hypokalaemia), fluid retention
- Cardiac arrhythmia and sudden death (especially with diuretics, low potassium, heart disease, fast infusion)
- Anaphylaxis (rare), seizures, infections; avascular necrosis with repeated pulses

## Contraindications
- Active uncontrolled infection, systemic fungal infection
- Caution: heart disease, renal failure, electrolyte imbalance, uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension, psychiatric disease

## Drug interactions
- Diuretics and amphotericin B (hypokalaemia → arrhythmia)
- Enzyme inducers reduce effect; CYP3A4 inhibitors increase it

## Monitoring
- Before each pulse: BP, pulse, ECG, electrolytes (K⁺), blood glucose, renal function, infection screen, pregnancy test
- During infusion: BP and cardiac monitoring; repeat glucose and K⁺ after

## Pregnancy & lactation
Partly inactivated by the placenta; use only for life-threatening disease in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Pulse = 500 mg–1 g over at least 1 h on 3 consecutive days
- Check K⁺ and ECG before each pulse
- Succinate (IV, soluble) vs acetate (depot, never IV)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.13 (pulse definition); Khopkar ch.8. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
